morphology.look_here_first: Use the erect dark purple-green to reddish-black stem together with oblong to oblanceolate coarsely serrate leaves and the very small terminal/leaf-opposed raceme; confirm with flower counts, pedicel bases, and capsule size rather than stem color alone.
diagnostic_traits: perennial herb about 15–55 cm; stems erect, purple-green to reddish black, apex never flexuous
leaves oblong to oblanceolate, base acute to obtuse, coarsely serrate with often recurved tooth tips
terminal racemes appearing leaf-opposed, with 2–5 staminate flowers
staminate pedicels 1.3–1.6 mm with persistent base 0.2–0.4 mm
4–5 stamens with filaments connate about half their length
capsules about 6–7 mm wide; seeds dark brown, about 2.5–3.2 mm
morphology.source_basis: Flora of North America treatment as reproduced by World Flora Online.

look_alikes: Tragia ramosa — usually linear-lanceolate to narrowly ovate leaves with truncate to weakly cordate bases; broader western range; key on reproductive characters and leaf base rather than habit alone.
Tragia brevispica — stems often flexuous and capsules often mature only one carpel; requires raceme/fruit inspection.
Tragia betonicifolia — compare leaf base, staminate-flower distribution, persistent pedicel bases and capsule dimensions.
